findings.summary: A class can be flagged on noise: there is no margin, and either metric alone is enough
findings.evidence: `better` is `s.landed_share > base.landed_share || first_pass a > b`, with a 3-job minimum. A setting at 3 of 3 beats a baseline at 9 of 10 and gets flagged. A setting with worse landed share but higher first-pass also counts as "helps". This matches the accepted reading, but a margin or interval test, or requiring landed share to be no worse, would cut false flags.

findings.summary: Helps names the first qualifying setting in sort order, not the best one
findings.evidence: `find` returns the first setting by model, then effort, that beats the baseline. When several do, the line names that one rather than the one with the highest landed share. Every setting is still listed beneath it, so the reader can see the figures.

findings.summary: Observational comparison: settings may differ in how hard their jobs were
findings.evidence: If higher effort is chosen for harder jobs within a class, the comparison is confounded. The verdict text "beat the default" reads as cause. The approach is acceptable for a status measure; the wording could say it is observed.

summary: The change meets the request. It adds a `specialization` function in crates/athena-core/src/status/planning.rs that reads the existing class_of_work field and groups dispatched request jobs by it, putting jobs with no class under "unclassified". Within each class it compares every producer model and effort against the most-used one, the baseline. A class is flagged "specialization helps" only when another setting with at least SPECIALIZATION_MIN_JOBS (3) jobs has a strictly higher landed share or first-pass rate than the baseline. Otherwise it reads "not enough jobs" or "no better setting". The result is stored in a new StatusView field, added to STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS, and printed by `athena status` as a section whose first line starts with `specialization`; nothing prints when there are no classes. OLY-R8-01 in docs/spec.toml now names this function as its mechanism, keeps owner Athena, and has a measure ending `status: specialization`. I ran the new core tests, the display test, the measure-label test, the xtask spec tests and the Hestia tests (which check every measure in the real spec); all pass. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test runs passed. Remaining concerns are minor and follow the accepted design. A 3-job setting can be flagged on noise because there is no margin. Either metric alone is enough to flag. The flagged setting is the first that qualifies, not the best. Only files on the expected list changed.
